title: FIFA Boss's Secret Plan to Sell Part of the World Cup Shocks His Own Team!
summary:
Imagine if someone tried to sell a slice of your favorite soccer tournament without telling anyone! That's what's happening at FIFA, the group that runs the World Cup. Two big bosses are very upset and speaking out.

Kevin Lamour, a top FIFA executive, says he and other staff were "deceived" — that means tricked — by FIFA President Gianni Infantino. Infantino wants to sell part of the World Cup's future profits to private investors for $20 billion. Lamour says this plan was kept secret and that staff "deserve better than contempt and intimidation" (being treated with disrespect and threats).

Another leader, Carlos Cordeiro, just quit his job as Infantino's senior adviser. He says the deal is "a bad deal for football" and that he never knew about the talks with a New York investment fund run by Joshua Kushner. Cordeiro used to be a banker, so he knows money. He says FIFA already has billions in savings and no debt, so selling a permanent stake makes no sense. "It is mortgaging football's future," he said — like borrowing money you can't pay back.

Infantino's plan would let investors own 20% of a new company that controls World Cups for men and women. He's offering each of FIFA's 211 member countries $20 million if they agree by September 19. But Lamour and Cordeiro want everyone to speak up and stop it. They say this decision should be for the love of the game, not for profit.
why_it_matters: If one person can secretly sell a part of your favorite tournament, decisions that affect millions of fans might be made without thinking about what they want or need.

background_read: FIFA is the organization that runs the World Cup, the most popular soccer tournament on Earth, which billions of people watch.
Gianni Infantino has been FIFA's president since 2016 and often proposes big changes to how the World Cup is managed and financed.
Joshua Kushner is a wealthy American investor whose investment fund would be involved in the secret deal, giving private investors a permanent share of future World Cup profits.
Article_Structure: WHO: FIFA President Gianni Infantino, executives Kevin Lamour and Carlos Cordeiro, and an investment fund run by Joshua Kushner.
WHAT: Infantino secretly plans to sell 20% of a company that controls men’s and women’s World Cups to private investors for $20 billion.
WHERE: Inside FIFA, with talks linked to a New York investment fund.
WHY: Lamour and Cordeiro say the plan was hidden, is a bad deal for football, and mortgages the sport’s future without proper openness.

perspectives.description: Some might say the huge payment would help develop soccer in poorer countries, since each of FIFA’s 211 members would get $20 million.
Lamour and Cordeiro argue the deal sells away future earnings forever, giving outside investors power over the game and treating staff with disrespect.
Large sports organizations often look for new ways to raise money, but doing it secretly can break trust and lead to big fights among its leaders.
